quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When should you do a pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle are more dangerous than on a car. Check your motorcycle before every ride to stay safe.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, what should you do?
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, sudden changes in speed or direction can cause a skid. Accelerate, shift, turn, and brake as smoothly as possible.

questions.question: When being passed, where should you position your motorcycle in the lane?
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed. Moving closer to the passing driver creates a dangerous situation.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
You must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red light. Stop completely and wait for a signal that allows you to turn.

questions.question: What should you look for when choosing a helmet?
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets DOT and state standards. It should fit snugly and have no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: What should your lane position NOT do?

options.text: Make you more visible to others.
Invite other drivers into your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers into your lane.
questions.explanation: Good lane positioning makes you more visible, helps you avoid hazards, and discourages other drivers from sharing your lane. It should also give you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: How should you approach a blind intersection?

options.text: Move to where other drivers can see you earliest.
Move closer to the traffic control device.
Move to the outside edge of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to where other drivers can see you earliest.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, position yourself so other drivers see you as soon as possible.

questions.question: What should you do about the oily strip in the center of a traffic lane?

options.text: Find the lane with less oil and grease.

questions.explanation: Avoid the oily strip in the center of lanes. Since it is usually about two feet wide, you can ride on either side and still stay in the center portion of the lane.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a slippery surface?

options.text: Avoid sudden moves to prevent skidding.
Travel on the shoulder to stay away from traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden moves to prevent skidding.
questions.explanation: Sudden changes in speed or direction on a slippery surface cause skids. Be smooth when you speed up, shift, turn, or brake.

questions.question: What clothing should you wear when riding?
questions.explanation: Wear bright clothing to be more visible while riding, even during the day. Reflective materials also help increase visibility.

questions.question: What can cause motorcycle collisions?
questions.explanation: Following too closely behind another vehicle, called tailgating, can cause motorcycle collisions. Always keep a safe distance between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: When should you inspect your motorcycle for safety?
questions.explanation: Always check your motorcycle before you ride. Small problems on a motorcycle are more dangerous than small problems on a car.

questions.question: If vehicles are on both sides of you, which lane position is safest?
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. A good rider changes position based on road and traffic conditions. The center position is usually safest when vehicles are on both sides of you.

questions.question: What is the best lane position to ride in?

options.text: There is no single best lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best lane position.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. A good rider changes position as conditions change.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers about traffic laws in that area. This sign means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: Which statement about eye protection is correct?

options.text: You don't need it if your motorcycle has a windshield.
You only need it in bad weather.
It should let you see clearly to both sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: It should let you see clearly to both sides.
questions.explanation: California law requires proper eye and face protection. A good face shield protects your whole face and lets you see clearly to both sides.

questions.question: What is NOT required on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Idaho requires all motorcycles to have fenders, brakes, headlight, horn, mirror, muffler, brake light, taillight, and reflectors. If you carry a passenger, you also need a passenger seat and footrests. A flag is not required.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The light will change to red soon.
The light will change to green soon.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light will change to red soon.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns you that the light will turn red. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection, continue through it.

questions.question: What does the SEE strategy stand for?
questions.explanation: Good riders use the SEE strategy to make safe decisions. SEE stands for Search, Evaluate, and Execute.

questions.question: What is a difference between goggles and a windshield?

options.text: Goggles protect from wind, but a windshield doesn't.
A windshield protects from wind, but goggles don't.
A windshield stops your eyes from watering better than goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles protect from wind, but a windshield doesn't.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes from the wind. Most windshields do not. A windshield is not a good substitute for goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: What lane position best prevents other vehicles from sharing your lane?

options.text: The left portion of the lane
The center portion of the lane
The right portion of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion of the lane
questions.explanation: Riding in the center of your lane discourages other drivers from squeezing in next to you. When you ride behind another vehicle, the center position makes you most visible in their rearview mirror.

questions.question: When you drink alcohol faster:

options.text: The alcohol leaves your body faster.
The alcohol builds up in your body faster.
The alcohol affects your body less.

questions.correctAnswerText: The alcohol builds up in your body faster.
questions.explanation: Your body removes alcohol at about one drink per hour. If you drink more than one drink in an hour, alcohol will still be in your body after that hour passes.

questions.question: When should you use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch?

options.text: The throttle is stuck and you cannot free it.
You start to lose control in a curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: The throttle is stuck and you cannot free it.
questions.explanation: If the throttle gets stuck, immediately use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch. This stops power to the rear wheel so you can safely pull off the road and stop.

questions.question: When can a motorcycle pass on the right?

options.text: If there is at least eight feet of clear pavement.
By riding on the shoulder of the road.
By riding on grass, if it is level.

questions.correctAnswerText: If there is at least eight feet of clear pavement.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle may pass on the right only if there is at least eight feet of clear pavement to the right of the vehicle being passed. Never leave the road to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: Experienced riders use SIPDE to stay aware of conditions around them. What does the "S" stand for?
questions.explanation: SIPDE is a five-step process experienced riders use to make decisions while riding. The letters stand for Scan, Identify, Predict, Decide, and Execute.
